findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted_attributes restriction, leaking domain for restricted users
findings.body: The new `website_name` attribute is added to the `attributes` list (line 43) but is not included in the `untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location, :website, :profile_background, :card_background` list (lines 105-111). That list is what hides sensitive profile fields (including `website`) from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. TL0 user viewed anonymously). Because `website_name` is derived from the same `website` data but is not covered by this restriction, an anonymous viewer who should not be able to see a TL0 user's website will still see the host/path derived from it via `website_name`. This defeats the existing privacy restriction and leaks information that `website` itself is meant to hide. The existing spec (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` untrusted_attributes list) doesn't check `website_name`, so this leak is not caught by tests.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by the serializer convention
findings.body: Every other conditional-inclusion method in this file follows the pattern `include_<attr>?` (e.g. `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_edit_history_public?`, `include_email?`). The new method is defined as `include_website_name` without the trailing `?` (line 153). ActiveModel::Serializer looks for `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to include an attribute; since this predicate name doesn't match, it's never invoked, and `website_name` falls back to the default (always included because it is listed in `attributes`). This means the intended guard (`website.present?`) silently has no effect, and in combination with the issue above, there is no server-side control at all over when `website_name` is exposed.

findings.title: No test verifies website_name is hidden for TL0/anonymous restricted users
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used in the "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" test (line 11) was not updated to include `:website_name`, even though this PR introduces that derived attribute from the same restricted `website` data. As a result, there is no test coverage asserting that `website_name` is also suppressed when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true, which would have caught the leak described above.
